description:
## What happens

A heredoc is a string literal, so it interpolates. `@doc` and `@moduledoc` need a literal string, so a doc that *describes* interpolation stops being one:

```
  @moduledoc """
  ... every interpolated value, since `"a#{x}b"` lexes to ...
  """
```

That heredoc lexes to a `Concat` expression rather than a binary, and the front door refuses it. Two messages, depending on where the attribute sits:

```
error[parse/expected-token]: compiler2 quoted front door expected protocol callback or attribute, got Concat
  --> runtime:StringChars.fz:20:14
20 |   @moduledoc """
   |              ^^^

error[parse/expected-token]: compiler2 quoted front door does not yet parse Concat at item position
```

## What is right about this

The refusal, and the span. It points at the `"""` that opened the heredoc, in the right file, at the right line. Nothing is silent and nothing miscompiles.

## What is wrong

The message names an internal node type. `Concat` is not a word in the language the author is writing; nothing connects it to the `#{...}` a few lines below, which is the actual cause and is not itself underlined. An author who has just written a paragraph of prose has no reason to suspect their documentation was parsed as an expression.

"does not yet parse" makes it worse in the other direction: it reads as an unimplemented feature, inviting the author to wait for support, when an interpolating doc attribute is not something that should ever be supported -- `@doc` takes a literal by definition.

## Acceptance

- An attribute given an interpolated string says so: that `@doc`/`@moduledoc` takes a literal string, that this one interpolates, and that `\#{` escapes the sigil in prose that describes it.
- The span covers the interpolation, not only the opening delimiter, when one is present.
- A fixture pins the diagnostic.

## Correction

This ticket previously claimed the module compiled silently and that two fixtures changed behaviour with nothing reported. That was wrong, and the error was mine: I diagnosed from fixture symptoms without ever compiling a program against the broken library, so I never saw the diagnostic the compiler was already emitting. The fixtures failed because the library module failed to parse, which is the system working. Re-priced from P1 to P3 accordingly.
title: A doc attribute whose heredoc interpolates is rejected by node type, not by explanation
